topics.lesson_subject: IPAM-managed firewall address objects with per-device unique subnet allocation
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: IPAM allocation is bound to firewall-address objects; type=ipam plus fabric-object and ipam-allocate-unique requests a distinct subnet per Security Fabric FortiGate instead of synchronized identical subnet values.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: IPAM pool/rule selection by object-name pattern -> address-object allocation -> optional VPN-gateway client-range consumption -> CSF distribution with unique allocation semantics -> policy reference.
topics.failure_class: Address-pool exhaustion, wrong IPAM rule match, shared subnet collision across Fabric members, VPN client pool overlap.
topics.evidence_pattern: Inspect IPAM subnet/rule allocations and the firewall address object on each FortiGate; compare actual subnet values across Fabric members. A successful object sync alone does not prove distinct allocation or free-pool capacity.
topics.remediation_path: Enable IPAM; define non-overlapping pools and address-name rules; verify object type and fabric-object; enable ipam-allocate-unique only where per-device allocation is intended; validate pool capacity and VPN range use before policy install.
topics.question_fingerprint: Given a Fabric object synced to two FortiGates, identify why identical address subnets appear and which IPAM allocation control makes each device unique.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: IPAM pool/rule decision feeding a Fabric firewall-address object that branches into FGT-A and FGT-B unique subnets, with optional VPN gateway consumer.
topics.semantic_overlap_decision: PASS: no matching firewall-address IPAM object allocation mechanism in the 369 historical fingerprints or the 12 earlier same-day topics; rejected overlay-orchestrator IPAM because that was a different, already-covered overlay address workflow.

topics.lesson_subject: Cisco pxGrid connected-user enrichment with Device Type and Session State
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiManager pxGrid connector imports Cisco ISE identity/security-group context and exposes endpoint Device Type and Session State fields for connected users.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: ISE pxGrid certificate-based client approval -> FortiManager connector session -> event/user-group import -> ADOM identity table -> Device Type/Session State filters and downstream policy use.
topics.failure_class: TLS client authentication/ISE approval failure, DNS resolution of ISE node FQDNs, missing Security Group, unsupported ISE session states ignored.
topics.evidence_pattern: Connected Users table and `diagnose system print connector <adom> pxgrid <connector_name> <filter>` show imported identities and session fields; an established TLS socket alone does not prove pxGrid authorization or accepted event state.
topics.remediation_path: Approve FortiManager in Cisco ISE pxGrid Services; trust the correct certificate; ensure DNS resolves every ISE node FQDN; define Security Group; check supported states (Started, Postured, Disconnected) and explicitly import/refresh.
topics.question_fingerprint: A pxGrid TLS session is established but FortiManager shows no users; distinguish ISE authorization, missing Security Group, and ignored session states.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Cisco ISE PAN/MnT and pxGrid nodes -> certificate/approval boundary -> FortiManager connector/ADOM -> connected-user records with Device Type and Session State.
topics.semantic_overlap_decision: PASS: no pxGrid connector or session-state enrichment topic in the historical or same-day inventories; certificate-renewal community item was retained as older scenario context only, not a recent primary source.

topics.lesson_subject: FortiAI Threat Posture Timeline: entity-scoped log and alert correlation over a selected time window
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiAI Endpoint Analysis Agent gathers related logs and alerts for an Asset Identity Center endpoint and summarizes traffic, sessions, threat score, highlights, and rationale over a selected timeframe.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Asset Identity record selection -> timeframe selection -> related log/alert retrieval across Fabric sources -> AI analysis -> timeline widgets/highlights -> PDF or incident action.
topics.failure_class: Missing FortiAI entitlement/administrator access, weak or incomplete entity identity correlation, wrong time window, absent source logs.
topics.evidence_pattern: Timeline displays source-device logs, alerts, traffic/sessions/threat score; changing the chart metric does not trigger new analysis, but changing timeframe fetches logs and runs analysis again. A summary is not raw-log completeness proof.
topics.remediation_path: Verify FortiAI license and administrator entitlement; confirm endpoint identity and source logging; select the correct timeframe before analysis; inspect source logs/highlights and attach evidence to an incident.
topics.question_fingerprint: An analyst changes Traffic to Threat Score and expects a fresh AI analysis; identify which UI action reruns the agent and which only changes the chart.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Multiple Fabric log/alert sources converge on an Asset Identity Center endpoint, then FortiAI analysis fans out to timeline, summary, highlights, PDF/incident outputs.
topics.semantic_overlap_decision: PASS: no Threat Posture Timeline mechanism in historical or same-day topics; distinguished from alert-centric FortiAI triage and AI Access Visibility topics.

topics.lesson_subject: DHCP snooping binding database as the shared trust source for Dynamic ARP Inspection and IPv4 source guard
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: DHCP snooping validates DHCP messages on untrusted ports and maintains IP/MAC/VLAN/interface lease bindings; DAI consumes bindings to reject invalid ARP; IPv4 source guard enforces allowed source IPs per port using dynamic or static bindings.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Trusted DHCP server/uplink -> client DHCP exchange on untrusted access port -> snooping validation and binding creation -> DAI ARP check and source-guard ingress check.
topics.failure_class: Rogue DHCP server, missing/stale binding, trusted-port misclassification, static endpoint absent from database, mode transition clearing bindings, hardware/model scale limit.
topics.evidence_pattern: DHCP snooping client/server DB and FortiGate-managed switch status command prove lease learning; DAI/source-guard counters/logs prove enforcement. A client DHCP lease alone does not prove ARP/source guard is active.
topics.remediation_path: Enable trusted-server list; enable snooping per VLAN; trust only legitimate server-facing ports; verify client DB; add static IP/MAC entries for non-DHCP hosts; enable DAI/source guard per port; plan monitor/enable transitions because entries may be cleared.
topics.question_fingerprint: A statically addressed printer is dropped by DAI despite being reachable before enforcement; identify the required static snooping binding and its port/VLAN constraints.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Trusted DHCP server uplink and untrusted client ports feed a snooping binding database; database feeds DAI ARP validation and per-port IPv4 source guard.
topics.semantic_overlap_decision: PASS: no DHCP snooping/DAI/source-guard binding-database lesson in prior reports; related FortiSwitch auto-topology lesson is not the same L2 trust database mechanism.

topics.lesson_subject: 6 GHz Standard Power operation: AFC location eligibility, country code, and channel grant lifecycle
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: AFC is a regulatory coordination service: a capable FortiAP supplies its physical location and receives an available-channel response before Standard Power 6 GHz operation; model and regulatory domain determine whether LPI fallback is possible.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: FortiGate country/region and AP model profile -> AP location source (GPS or configured static position) -> AFC request with location -> AFC available-channel response -> radio channel/power operation.
topics.failure_class: Incorrect country code, unavailable/invalid GPS position, unsupported model power mode, AFC response unavailable, region not requiring AFC, wrong channel-width/profile constraints.
topics.evidence_pattern: Community diagnostic `cw_diag -c afc status`, AFC request/response dumps, console logs, and FortiGate WTP position type prove different stages; GPS position alone does not prove AFC authorization or channel grant.
topics.remediation_path: Set the correct country/region and indoor/outdoor designation; verify model-specific antenna/GNSS capability; confirm GPS/static position and AFC status/response; use LPI only on models/regulatory domains that permit it; avoid treating 6 GHz absence as generic RF interference.
topics.question_fingerprint: A FAP443K in a US outdoor deployment has no 6 GHz channel; distinguish missing AFC location/grant from the FAP441K LPI fallback that is not available to FAP443K.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiGate country/profile and FortiAP location source feed AFC request/response service, which gates the 6 GHz radio's channel and power mode.
topics.semantic_overlap_decision: PASS with narrow scope: historical LoWi lesson covered how coordinates are calculated; today's lesson covers regulatory AFC channel authorization and Standard Power eligibility, using LoWi/GPS only as a prerequisite, not reteaching location trilateration.

topics.lesson_subject: Access Point Management: DHCP lease authorization and StaticIPAddress event enforcement for bridged AP clients
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC controls hosts behind bridged APs by maintaining authorized/unauthorized DHCP pools, mapping AP-facing switch ports, and checking client MAC addresses against its DHCP lease file; missing leases generate StaticIPAddress events.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: AP discovered as bridge -> upstream switch port assigned to AP Management group -> client DHCP -> lease/authorized MAC database -> valid DNS for authorized host or NAC DNS redirect for unauthorized host -> event/alarm mapping for static IP.
topics.failure_class: AP remains classified as bridge, AP uplink misidentified, port not in AP Management group, DHCP lease mismatch, static-IP event not mapped, wrong FortiNAC product/version.
topics.evidence_pattern: DHCP lease file membership and StaticIPAddress event prove the host's MAC is or is not represented in NAC-managed leases; an AP being discovered does not prove its downstream clients are controlled.
topics.remediation_path: Configure AP Management view/VLAN/IP pools in Configuration Wizard; remove AP from Bridging Devices group; disable incorrect user-defined uplink; resync interfaces; add AP-facing switch port to AP Management group; map StaticIPAddress event to alarm/action.
topics.question_fingerprint: A bridged AP is discovered but clients with static IPs bypass expected controls; identify the DHCP lease-file check and StaticIPAddress event path.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Bridged AP behind managed switch port branches authorized and unauthorized clients through FortiNAC DHCP/lease state, DNS steering, and StaticIPAddress alarm path.
topics.semantic_overlap_decision: PASS: no AP-management DHCP lease authorization lesson in the 30-day FortiNAC history; explicit version boundary: Access Point Management was removed from FortiNAC-F 7.6, so this applies to FortiNAC 9.4 only.

topics.lesson_subject: Administrator GUI MFA: individual versus global SMS/email token enforcement
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC-F 7.6.5 adds administrator GUI MFA using SMS or email one-time tokens, with per-administrator settings or global enforcement and default-country-code inheritance.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Admin username/password -> individual/global MFA policy evaluation -> OTP delivery by SMS or email -> token timeout validation -> administrator GUI session.
topics.failure_class: No phone/email attribute, wrong country code, delivery gateway failure, expired token, global policy enabled unexpectedly, administrator-level override mismatch.
topics.evidence_pattern: Administrator MFA settings and global policy show enforcement scope; delivery log/gateway status and token acceptance show second-factor completion. Password success alone does not prove MFA completed.
topics.remediation_path: Set per-admin contact data and MFA preference; configure global SMS/email only when intended; set default country code and token timeout; verify REST SMS gateway when used; reset MFA settings only as a recovery operation.
topics.question_fingerprint: One administrator has no personal country code while global SMS MFA is enabled; determine which country code is used and why another administrator may differ.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Administrator login splits into individual/global MFA policy selection, then SMS/email OTP provider and token-timeout gate before GUI session issuance.
topics.semantic_overlap_decision: PASS: no FortiNAC-F administrator GUI MFA workflow in the historical or same-day inventory; distinct from RADIUS EAP-TLS/endpoint MFA and FortiSwitch FIDO2 administrator authentication.

topics.lesson_subject: REST API self-service provisioning of external SAML IdP resources with Swagger-discovered schemas
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiAuthenticator 8.0.2 adds REST resources `/remotesamlservers/` and `/samlidpusersources/` for self-service external IdP creation and exposes API schemas through built-in Swagger UI at `/api/v2/docs`.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Provisioning client authenticates to FAC REST API -> discovers method/schema in Swagger -> creates remote SAML server and IdP user-source resources -> links IdP source to SAML user/group or SP workflow -> validates metadata/certificate and user-source binding.
topics.failure_class: Wrong API version/schema, missing API permission, incomplete remote IdP metadata/certificate, orphaned user-source object, duplicate resource or unsupported field assumptions.
topics.evidence_pattern: Swagger schema and API response confirm accepted resource fields and object creation; a created REST object does not prove a valid SAML trust relationship or successful assertion/group mapping.
topics.remediation_path: Use the built-in Swagger UI for exact methods and required fields; use least-privilege API credentials; create remote SAML server and user-source resources in dependency order; validate entity ID, ACS/metadata, signing certificate, and group-source mapping with an end-to-end SAML test.
topics.question_fingerprint: An automation creates a remote SAML server but SAML user groups remain empty; identify the separate IdP user-source resource and the evidence needed beyond HTTP success.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: External IdP provisioning client -> FAC REST API/Swagger -> remote SAML server object and SAML IdP user-source object -> SAML trust and user/group consumption.
topics.semantic_overlap_decision: PASS: no REST API external-IdP provisioning resource workflow in historical or same-day topics; distinct from SAML proxy authentication and OAuth/PKCE login flows.

topics.lesson_subject: Non-TOTP 2FA challenges issued by SSH targets through the WebSSH launcher
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: WebSSH relays a target SSH server's interactive second-factor challenge to the FortiPAM console and allows manual entry of real-time FortiToken/SMS/email/third-party authenticator codes; FortiPAM does not need a built-in TOTP secret for the target.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: User launches secret -> WebSSH establishes SSH to target -> target emits interactive 2FA prompt -> WebSSH renders prompt -> user enters code or requests push -> target validates factor -> shell opens.
topics.failure_class: Challenge not relayed because secret lacks required SSH service/filter/auto-password/Target-Only template prerequisites; incorrect token; target-specific challenge incompatibility.
topics.evidence_pattern: Prompt from the SSH target and target authentication logs prove the challenge was reached; FortiPAM login success does not prove target second factor; wrong token cannot be retried in same SSH connection.
topics.remediation_path: Confirm target-side 2FA challenge; enable SSH service with a filter (empty filter acceptable), SSH Auto-Password, or Target-Only template as required for SMS/email; prefer manual code entry; close and relaunch after an incorrect code.
topics.question_fingerprint: A WebSSH session displays a target-side OTP prompt but SMS push is not relayed; identify the secret configuration prerequisite and the no-retry behavior.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiPAM secret/launcher opens SSH to target; target challenge flows back through WebSSH to user, and entered OTP is returned to target for validation.
topics.semantic_overlap_decision: PASS: historical FortiPAM SSH command filters and RDP Kerberos topics do not cover target-issued non-TOTP WebSSH challenge relay.

topics.lesson_subject: Asynchronous incident triggering-events API: queryId job lifecycle
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: The triggering-events retrieval API changes from synchronous response to an asynchronous job model with start, progress, and result endpoints keyed by queryId.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Client submits incidentId/timeFrom/timeTo to `/pub/incident/triggeringEvents/start` -> receives queryId -> polls `/progress/{queryId}` -> when progress is 100%, retrieves `/result/{queryId}`.
topics.failure_class: Client timeout from old synchronous assumptions, lost queryId, polling too aggressively, retrieving result before completion, mismatched incident/time window.
topics.evidence_pattern: Start response queryId proves job acceptance; progress percentage proves job state; result payload proves retrieval completion. HTTP success from start is not proof that triggering events are ready.
topics.remediation_path: Implement asynchronous orchestration; persist queryId; poll progress with bounded backoff; request result only after 100%; correlate incidentId/time window and handle transport retries without creating duplicate jobs.
topics.question_fingerprint: A SIEM integration receives queryId but an empty triggering-event result immediately; identify the required progress/result sequence.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: API client -> start endpoint -> queryId job store -> progress polling -> result endpoint -> incident evidence consumer.
topics.semantic_overlap_decision: PASS: no asynchronous triggering-events query lifecycle in the FortiSIEM history; distinct from Native Case API, ticketing, and watchlist lookup topics.

topics.lesson_subject: Private Proxy steering over Branch On-ramp: encrypted proxy transport for unmanaged endpoints
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Private Proxy provides HTTP/HTTPS proxy steering for clients without FortiClient by sending traffic to an on-prem Branch On-ramp device, then through an encrypted IPsec tunnel to FortiSASE; optional SPA provides private-resource access.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Proxy client PAC/manual settings -> private proxy primary/secondary IP on Branch On-ramp nodes -> on-ramp firewall and BGP routing -> IPsec tunnel to FortiSASE PoP -> proxy security policy -> Internet or optional SPA private resource.
topics.failure_class: Select-availability feature not enabled, Branch On-ramp license/IP missing, BGP not configured first, proxy client points to wrong IP, deep-inspection CA absent, NAT breaks IP-based identity, incompatible proxy migration state.
topics.evidence_pattern: Branch On-ramp tunnel/route state and FortiSASE proxy logs show traffic reached the service; client proxy configuration alone does not prove encrypted tunnel steering or user identity. With IP-based auth, NAT must be disabled and SSO configured.
topics.remediation_path: Request select availability; license/configure Branch On-ramp and dedicated IP; establish BGP before enabling; configure primary/secondary proxy IPs on all nodes; set PAC/manual proxy on clients; install FortiSASE CA for deep inspection; preserve source IP for IP-based auth.
topics.question_fingerprint: A private proxy client reaches the on-ramp but FortiSASE logs cannot distinguish users; identify the SSO plus no-NAT condition for IP-based identity.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Unmanaged LAN proxy clients -> on-prem Branch On-ramp -> encrypted IPsec tunnel/BGP -> FortiSASE PoP proxy -> Internet and optional SPA hub/private apps.
topics.semantic_overlap_decision: PASS: no Private Proxy steering method in historical or same-day topics; distinct from endpoint VPN auto-connect, source-IP anchoring, SPA hub endpoint-to-endpoint, and FortiSASE central management.

topics.lesson_subject: SD-WAN packet-duplication bandwidth thresholds across overlay or underlay interfaces
topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiOS 8.0 evaluates member bandwidth before duplicating traffic and stops duplication when upstream, downstream, or bidirectional utilization exceeds a configured threshold measured on overlay or underlay.
topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: SD-WAN rule selects duplication-capable members -> member bandwidth source selected (overlay/underlay) -> directional threshold evaluation -> duplicate while below threshold -> stop extra copies above threshold while normal forwarding remains.
topics.failure_class: Wrong bandwidth measurement layer, incorrect direction threshold, shared underlay utilization ignored by overlay-only measurement, threshold unit misread, duplicate count/topology assumptions.
topics.evidence_pattern: Per-member interface counters and packet captures show actual utilization and duplicate copies; a healthy SLA does not prove duplication threshold is below limit, and cessation of duplicates does not imply original traffic is dropped.
topics.remediation_path: Choose overlay versus underlay measurement deliberately; configure up/down/bi thresholds in KB/s per member; verify member-to-underlay mapping and duplication-max-num; test below/above threshold with packet captures and interface counters.
topics.question_fingerprint: Two overlays share one congested physical underlay; identify why underlay-based thresholding stops duplication on both even if each overlay's own counter appears low.
topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Traffic classifier and SD-WAN duplication rule fan out across multiple overlay members mapped to shared underlay links; directional utilization gate controls duplicate-copy branches.
topics.semantic_overlap_decision: PASS: no bandwidth-gated packet duplication threshold in the historical or same-day inventory; distinct from ToS-based duplication, FEC, and monthly quota steering.
